groups.summary: The README was 215 lines of reference-grade prose. The opening paragraph ran ten sentences and mixed the pitch with the systemd slice name and the workspace identifier, Install carried the complete dependency list, and "What it does" was eight dense paragraphs down to nftables sets and socket2 events. The features that would sell the plugin were in there, but a reader had to mine for them.
groups.title: A reference manual on the front page

groups.summary: A person landing on the repository page should be able to tell in about a minute what the plugin does and whether they want it. The reference material stays in the repository: it moves out of the README into the docs, so the README becomes the pitch and the quick path in, and the docs stay the complete account.
groups.title: The README pitches, the docs keep the full account

The site-block line describes what a listed site typed into the work browser does over HTTPS: the page fails to load and a "Blocked here" banner offers to open it in the space, and the known-gaps sentence scopes the banner-only limit to HTTPS. changeWalkthrough.thesis: The README was a 215-line reference manual; a visitor had to mine it to learn what the plugin does. It is now an 83-line pitch: one sentence that the plugin makes distractions hard to reach, seven features led by the site block and the lock, six maintainer-approved screenshots beside their features, and a short Install section. The site-block line shows what a listed site does over HTTPS, a "Blocked here" banner, since browsers reach nearly every site that way. Every reference fact the README held moved to docs/reference.md or docs/CONTRIBUTING.md, except the 2.x upgrade section and the pre-2.1.0 id note, which are dropped. No code, test, or manifest changes.
